questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In the parabola $y^2=4 a x$ the length of the latus rectum is 6 units and there is a chord passing through its vertex and the negative end of the latus rectum. Then the equation of the chord is
questions.solution:
The equation of the parabola is $y^2 = 4ax$. The length of the latus rectum is given as $4a = 6$, which implies $a = \dfrac{6}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

The coordinates of the vertex are $(0, 0)$. The endpoints of the latus rectum are $(a, 2a)$ and $(a, -2a)$. The negative end of the latus rectum is $(a, -2a)$.

Substituting $a = \dfrac{3}{2}$, the coordinates of the negative end of the latus rectum are $(\dfrac{3}{2}, -2 \times \dfrac{3}{2}) = (\dfrac{3}{2}, -3)$.

The chord passes through the vertex $(0, 0)$ and the point $(\dfrac{3}{2}, -3)$. The slope $m$ of this chord is $m = \dfrac{-3 - 0}{\dfrac{3}{2} - 0} = \dfrac{-3}{\dfrac{3}{2}} = -2$.

The equation of the line passing through the origin with slope $m = -2$ is $y = -2x$, which can be rewritten as $2x + y = 0$.

Answer: $2 x+y=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The tangents drawn at the extremities of a focal chord of the parabola $y^{2}=16 x$
questions.solution:
The tangent at the extremities of a focal chord of a parabola intersect at right angles on the directrix.
Now, equation of parabola is $y^{2}=16 x$.
So, its directrix is $x=-4$ or $x+4$.
So, tangent intersect on the line $x+4=0$.

questions.q: The ends of the latusrectum of the parabola $x^{2}+10 x-16 y+25=0$ are
questions.solution:
Given, equation of parabola is

x^{2}+10 x-16 y+25=0

It can be rewritten as

(x+5)^{2}=16 y

Here $a=4$ and vertex $\equiv(-5,0)$
and focus $=(-5,4)$
So, $y$-coordinate of ends of latusrectum will be 4 .
Putting in equation, we have
$(x+5)^{2}=16 \times 4=64\Rightarrow \quad x+5=\pm 8$
So, $\quad x=3,-13$
Substituting $x$ in Eq. (i), we get $y=4,4$
Hence, ends of latusrectum will be $(3,4)$ and $(-13,4)$.

questions.q: Find the point on the curve $y=x^{2}$, where the slope of the tangent is equal to the $x$ coordinate of the point.
questions.solution:
Let the required point be $\boldsymbol{P}\left(x_{1}, y_{1}\right)$ 
The given curve is $y=x^{2}...(i)$
Differentiating Eq. (i) w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\frac{d y}{d x}=2 x \Rightarrow$ Slope of tangent at $P\left(x_{1}, y_{1}\right)=2 x$
But the slope of tangent at
$\begin{aligned}
& P\left(x_{1}, y_{1}\right)=x \text {-coordinate of } P \\
\Rightarrow & 2 x_{1}=x_{1} \Rightarrow 2 x_{1}-x_{1}=0 \\
\Rightarrow & x_{1}=0
\end{aligned}$
As $P\left(x_{1}, y_{1}\right)$ lies on the curve, we get $y_{1}=x_{1}^{2} \Rightarrow y_{1}=0$
Hence, the required point is $(0, J)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the parabola with vertex at $(-1,1)$ and focus $(2,1)$ is
questions.solution:
Given, vertex of the parabola $(h, k)=(-1,1)$ and its focus is
$(a+h, k)=(2,1) \text { or } a+h=2 \Rightarrow a=3$
We know that as the $y$-coordinate of vertex and focus are same,therefore axis of parabola is parallel to $X$-axis. Thus, equation of parabola is
$\begin{gathered}
(y-k)^{2}=4 a(x-h) \\
(y-1)^{2}=4 \times 3(x+1) \\
(y-1)^{2}=12 x+12 \\
y^{2}+1-2 y=12 x+12 \\
y^{2}-12 x-2 y-11=0
\end{gathered}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angle between the curve $y^{2}=4 a x$ and $a y=2 x^{2}$ is
questions.solution:
We have, $\quad y^{2}=4 a x \quad \text{...(i)}$
and
$a y=2 x^{2} \quad \text{...(ii)}$
Solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

x=a \text { and } y=2 a

Differentiating Eq. (i) w.r.t. $x$, we get
$2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=4 a$
Now, $\quad\left[\frac{d y}{d x}\right]_{(a, 2 a)}=\frac{4 a}{2(2 a)}=1\Rightarrow \quad m_{1}=1$
Now, differentiating Eq. (ii) w.r.t. $x$, we get

\begin{gathered}
a \frac{d y}{d x}=4 x \Rightarrow\left[\frac{d y}{d x}\right]_{(a, 2 a)}=\frac{4 a}{a}=4 \\
\Rightarrow \quad m_{2}=4
\end{gathered}

$\because$ Angle between curves is equal to angle between their tangents.

\begin{aligned}
& \tan \theta\left|\frac{m_{2}-m_{1}}{1+m_{1} m_{2}}\right| \Rightarrow \tan \theta=\left|\frac{4-1}{1+4 \times(1)}\right| \\
\Rightarrow & \tan \theta=\frac{3}{5} \Rightarrow \theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)
\end{aligned}

questions.q: The equation of the lines joining the vertex of the parabola $y^{2}=6 x$ to the point on it which have abscissa 24 are
questions.solution:
Given, equation of parabola is $y^{2}=6 x$
Substitute $x=24y^{2}=6 \times 24$
y=\pm \sqrt{6 \times 24}=\pm \sqrt{6 \times 6 \times 4}=\pm(6 \times 2)=\pm 12

$\therefore$ Point on the parabola is $(24,12),(24,-12)$ vertex of given parabola is $(0,0)$.
$\therefore$ Equation of lines passing through $(0,0)$ and $(24,12)$, $(24,-12)$ is

y=\frac{12}{24} x, y=\frac{-12}{24} x

$\Rightarrow \quad 2 y-x=0,2 y+x=0\Rightarrow \quad 2 y \pm x=0$ are required equations of lines.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $(0,6)$ and $(0,3)$ are respectively the vertex and focus of a parabola, then its equation is
questions.solution:
The vertex and focus of the parabola are $(0,6)$ and $(0,3)$ respectively.
Clearly, axis is $Y$-axis.
$\therefore$ Latusrectum $=4$ (Distance between vertex and focus)

=4 \sqrt{(0-0)^{2}+(6-3)^{2}}=12

Also, the vertex is on the right hand side of the focus, so the parabola opens downward.
Hence, equation of the parabola is

\begin{aligned}
(x-0)^{2} &=-12(y-6) \\
x^{2} &=-12 y+72 \\
\Rightarrow \quad & x^{2}+12 y &=72
\end{aligned}

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The parametric equation of a parabola is $x=t^{2}+1, y=2 t+1$. The cartesian equation of its directrix is
questions.solution:
Given that, $x=t^{2}+1 \Rightarrow x-1=t^{2}$
and $\quad y=2 t+1 \Rightarrow y-1=2 t$
Now, $\quad(y-1)^{2}=4 t^{2}=4(x-1)(y-1)^{2}=4(x-1)$
So, $x-1=-1\Rightarrow \quad x=0$
